note: The configuration value for lxc.time.offset.boot is input-controlled and is parsed into offset plus a residual unit stored in the local stack buffer buf.
strtoll parses the leading integer from the input string and sets remaining to point at the input-controlled unit suffix.

For a non-empty residual shorter than residual_len, the suffix bytes are copied but the destination buffer is neither zero-filled nor explicitly NUL-terminated; the safety obligation is that len must leave a written terminator byte before treating residual as a C string.
The unterminated buf produced by lxc_safe_int64_residual is passed to the whitespace-trimming helper as a C string.

strlen(buffer) requires a NUL-terminated initialized string, but buf contains only the copied suffix bytes and an uninitialized byte, so strlen reads uninitialized stack data while searching for a terminator.
